title: KIA Forces Kill 40 SAC Troops and Capture 1 in Shwegu Township Battle — SAC Armored Column Repulsed Despite 1,000+ Reinforcements
detail: Kachin Independence Army (KIA) forces fighting the SAC armored reinforcement column in Shwegu Township, Kachin State, killed approximately 40 junta soldiers and captured one more by May 4, 2026, according to MoeMaKa CDM News. The engagement is among the most significant KIA combat actions of 2026, coming in response to the junta's deployment of more than 1,000 reinforcements — including tanks — into Shwegu from May 2. The KIA's ability to inflict heavy casualties on an armored, numerically superior SAC column demonstrates the resistance's improving anti-armor capability and tactical effectiveness in Kachin State's terrain. The Shwegu battle also reflects the KIA's strategic objective of preserving its operational corridor between Kachin State and northern Sagaing Region, which the junta's reinforced Shwegu deployment was designed to sever. MoeMaKa also noted that resistance forces struck military commission troops in Myingyan and Myaing during the same period, suggesting coordinated multi-front operations. The Shwegu battle casualties are consistent with the KIA's record of inflicting heavy losses on junta columns throughout its April 2026 multi-axis offensive (including the 40 militia killed in the Hpakant ambush on April 19 and the ~70-man column scattered in Putao on April 29).

media.caption: KIA kills 40 SAC troops and captures 1 in Shwegu Township battle (Kachin State) — SAC armored reinforcement column of 1,000+ repulsed with heavy casualties, May 4, 2026

title: KNLA Brigade 4 and Allies Capture Htee Khee Junta Operation Base on Thai-Myanmar Border — SAC Troops Flee Into Thailand After Week of Fighting
detail: Karen National Liberation Army (KNLA) Brigade 4 and allied resistance forces captured the junta's Htee Khee operational command base near the Thai-Myanmar border in Dawei Township, Tanintharyi Region, after approximately one week of fighting, with junta soldiers reportedly fleeing into Thailand. The Htee Khee capture follows KNLA's seizure of the Htee Hta strategic camp (approximately 5 miles from Htee Khee) on April 19, 2026 — suggesting a deliberate phased KNLA campaign to clear the entire Tanintharyi-Thailand border area of junta positions. The capture of Htee Khee is strategically significant: it represents another KNLA gain along the critical Thai-Myanmar border corridor, where the resistance has been progressively dismantling SAC outposts since 2024. It follows the KNLA's November 2025 capture of the Mawdaung/Singkhon Pass trade hub and the April 27 assault on Waw Lay military base near Myawaddy. The pattern of SAC troops fleeing into Thai territory mirrors the diplomatic tensions from the April 20 KNU hospital strike, where a bomb landed in Mae Hong Son Province, and heightens Thai-Myanmar border security concerns. Myanmar Now and the Myanmar Peace Monitor documented the Htee Khee capture as one of three junta outposts seized by KNLA and allied forces in this period.

media.caption: KNLA Brigade 4 captures Htee Khee junta operation base on Thai-Myanmar border (Tanintharyi Region) — SAC troops flee into Thailand after week of fighting, May 2026

title: SAC Attacks Kill 7 Civilians, Injure 6, and Destroy 90+ Homes Across Ler Doh, Natthalin, and Hpakant on May 4
detail: Myanmar's military junta killed seven civilians and injured six more while destroying more than 90 homes across three locations on May 4, 2026, according to MoeMaKa CDM News. The attacks occurred in Ler Doh Township (Kayah/Karenni State), Natthalin Township (Bago Region), and the Hpakant area (Kachin State), indicating the breadth of the junta's simultaneous civilian-targeting across multiple regions on a single day. Hpakant has been the site of sustained KIA-junta fighting throughout April-May 2026, including the May 2-4 Shwegu battle; the May 4 Hpakant civilian attacks are consistent with the SAC's pattern of retaliatory collective punishment against civilians in areas of active KIA resistance operations. The 90+ homes destroyed continues the systematic village burning campaign documented across Sagaing, Magway, and now Karenni and Bago regions. MoeMaKa noted these civilian attacks occurred on the same day as World Press Freedom Day events, with 47 journalists remaining in SAC detention as of May 3-4.

media.caption: SAC attacks kill 7 civilians, injure 6, and destroy 90+ homes in Ler Doh, Natthalin, and Hpakant — May 4, 2026 daily toll across Kayah, Bago, and Kachin states
